newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tight world grain stocks a bull point - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tight world grain stocks a bull point - Grainco.

text.p: An historically tight world feed grain stock position is likely to support the grains market somewhat in the longer-term, Rob Brealey, trading manager of Queensland grain co-operative Grainco, said in a weekly report.
Any problems with new season crops in the major producing or exporting countries would be bullish, he said.
Increased production forecasts by the USDA last week were bearish for short-term values, but the underlying fundamental remained that world feed grain stocks were tight, he said.
Australia's domestic grains market, still quiet in the past week, would continue to watch the U.S. for any early frost which could reduce the size of the corn crop.
It would also watch the size of feed wheat and feed barley crops in Queensland and New South Wales in Australia, he said.
Australia's domestic feed barley market appeared to be sitting on its hands, with growers and domestic consumers reluctant participants at current levels, he said.

"With the liklihood of a sizeable barley crop and the probability of feed wheat pressuring values at harvest, we will reach a point where sellers decide that storing the grain is a better short to medium term option than selling for the sake of selling," Brealey said.

The Australian malting barley crop continued to develop under favourable conditions, with the majority of the southern Queensland crop looking for rain by the end of September in order to achieve Australia's first export surplus in many years, he said.

The cottonseed market was again relatively inactive over the past week. The USDA crop production report, which reduced estimates of cotton lint and seed production, placed Australian cottonseed in a favourable position to consolidate export market gains made this season, Brealey said.
